mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with increased corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to reduced output and lower earnings.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 1% MoM and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points simultaneously over the past month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp simultaneously, and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% over 3 months and 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by more than 25bps and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% quarter-over-quarter and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth is above 2% annualized, it signals stagflationary pressures, which typically lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 1% QoQ and CPIAUCSL growth is above 2% annualized, and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
